claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived from approximately 185 to 253 CE.
Origen was born in Alexandria, Egypt, and died in Tyre, Phoenicia around 254 CE.
Origen was a prolific writer who wrote roughly 2,000 treatises in multiple branches of theology, including textual criticism, biblical exegesis and hermeneutics, homiletics, and spirituality.
Origen founded the Christian School of Caesarea, where he taught logic, cosmology, natural history, and theology.
Origen was tortured for his faith during the Decian persecution in 250 and died three to four years later from his injuries.
Origen's greatest work is the Hexapla, which is a synopsis of six versions of the Old Testament.
Origen wrote commentaries on almost every book of the Bible, of which only fragments survive today.
The Fragmenta in librum primum Regnorum survives as fragments preserved in catenas, specifically in catenas on Samuel and Kings and in catenas on the Song of Songs.

Origen compared the LXX text at his disposal with the Hebrew text in his text-critical work, the Hexapla, adding readings from later Greek versions marked with an asterisk when the Hebrew included material not in the LXX, and marking LXX readings not in the Hebrew with an obelos.
The Hexaplaric text derived from Origen's Hexapla became a distinct text form, though it is not found in a pure form in any manuscript of 1 Samuel.
Origen was one of the most influential and controversial figures in early Christian theology, apologetics, and asceticism.
